newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate down to 12.029 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 91-day T-bill rate down to 12.029 pct.

text.p: The average yield for the Philippines' benchmark 91-day Treasury bills fell to 12.029 percent at Monday's regular auction of government securities from 12.074 percent last week, the Bureau of Treasury said.
The average yield on the 182-day bills also dipped to 12.415 percent from 12.418. The yield on the 364-day bills slipped to 13.015 percent from 13.082.
The auction drew tenders worth 13.025 billion pesos, of which 6.0 billion pesos were accepted.
The 364-day bill drew bids totalling 5.495 billion pesos after the government last week said it was cutting its weekly volume of these mbills to 2.5 billion pesos from 3.5 billion.

The 91-day bills, of which 1.5 billion pesos were awarded, had tenders worth 4.090 billion pesos. The 182-day bills generated bids worth 3.440 billion pesos, of which 2.000 billion pesos were accepted.
Traders said the decline in interest rates is in line with expectations of lower inflation for the rest of the year.

Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said he expects inflation to fall below 6.5 percent in September. The latest year-on-year inflation was 8.9 percent in July. The August inflation rate will be announced next week.
